title: Improved Bounds for Reward-Agnostic and Reward-Free Exploration
claim: A layered hard-instance construction with deterministic action classes and probabilistic transitions forces any exploration algorithm to need many samples.
layout: Single graph, left-to-right layers of circular nodes, dashed versus solid arrows
description: A single state-transition diagram of a multi-state MDP used for a lower-bound construction. Circular nodes labeled S with superscripts and subscripts sit in three layers from left to right. One root node, S^0_1, has a green self-loop. A blue arrow and a red arrow run from it to the two middle nodes, S^1_1 and S^1_2. Dashed black arrows run from each middle node to all four right-hand nodes, S^2_1 through S^2_4, and they cross heavily in the middle of the figure. Each right-hand node has a thick black self-loop. Solid arrows mean deterministic transitions, dashed arrows mean probabilistic ones, and the blue, red and green colors mark classes of deterministic actions. The eye goes first to the colored arrows at the left, then to the dense dashed fan-out.
caption: Multiple states MDP construction for lower bound. Solid lines represent deterministic transition, and dashed lines represent probabilistic transitions. Blue, red and green represent classes of deterministic actions (see [ref]).
abstract: We study reward-free and reward-agnostic exploration in episodic finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs), where an agent explores an unknown environment without observing external rewards. Reward-free exploration aims to enable $Îµ$-optimal policies for any reward revealed after exploration, while reward-agnostic exploration targets $Îµ$-optimality for rewards drawn from a small finite class. In the reward-agnostic setting, Li, Yan, Chen, and Fan achieve minimax sample complexity, but only for restrictively small accuracy parameter $Îµ$. We propose a new algorithm that significantly relaxes the requirement on $Îµ$. Our approach is novel and of technical interest by itself. Our algorithm employs an online learning procedure with carefully designed rewards to construct an exploration policy, which is used to gather data sufficient for accurate dynamics estimation and subsequent computation of an $Îµ$-optimal policy once the reward is revealed. Finally, we establish a tight lower bound for reward-free exploration, closing the gap between known upper and lower bounds.
